html:
The battle fought on 18 June 1815 near Waterloo, south of Brussels in today's Belgium, where Napoleon was finally defeated. It ended the Napoleonic Wars.

Napoleon had been sent into exile on Elba in 1814. In March 1815 he escaped, landed in France and took back power without a fight, the start of the Hundred Days. The allies, then meeting at the Congress of Vienna, declared war on him. He marched north to beat their armies before they could join.

At Waterloo a British led army of British, Dutch, Belgian and German troops under the Duke of Wellington held a ridge all day against French attacks. In the afternoon the Prussian army under Blücher arrived on the French flank, and in the evening the French broke. Some 50,000 men were killed or wounded.

Napoleon abdicated again and was exiled to the far Atlantic island of Saint Helena, where he died in 1821. The peace settled at Vienna lasted, with few big wars, for decades. "Waterloo" became a word for final defeat.
sum: The battle fought on 18 June 1815 near Waterloo, south of Brussels in today's Belgium, where Napoleon was finally defeated. It ended the Napoleonic Wars.
